EO 7155 (August 23, 1935) exempts Wilbur John Carr, an Assistant Secretary of State, and continues him in the service 'for such time as may be deemed necessary, not in excess of five years from October 31, 1935.' The text fixes only an outer bound, October 31, 1940 (the computed candidate of the machine own-terms lead); the exemption ended earlier if Carr left the service or his continuance ceased to be deemed necessary. A not-later-than bound is not a first-end date (jobs/claim-kit/BATCH.md), and the evidence ruling of 2026-10-28 allows an interval only when evidence shows the event happened in it. No held source records the date Carr left the federal service, his retirement or death, or any determination ending his continuance; the register title search and the name and citation searches of held order texts found no later order naming him. Needed: a held record of the date Carr left the service (for example a Department of State Register or Foreign Service List entry, a retirement record or an official notice), or a held determination that ended the exemption.
